analysis.title: Alcon Inc. (ALCC.S): Q3 26 topline growth slightly below expectations; FY26 guidance range tightened
key_insights: Alcon Q3 26 constant currency revenue growth decelerated to 5.2% versus consensus of +6%, a fairly broad-based miss across divisions. Implantables, Equipment and Ocular Health each grew 2-3pts below consensus.
Consumables was the one bright spot, growing 6% (consensus 5.1%) on procedure volume, price increases and Valeda consumables.
After FX, Q3 26 revenue was $2,717m, -1% versus consensus.

Core gross margin expanded to 65.7% (+280bp Y/Y, +70bp Y/Y excluding $58m of tariff refunds). The gross profit beat was offset by higher opex, notably a step up in marketing, leaving core EBIT of $592m in line with consensus.
Core EPS of 0.92 was 6% ahead of consensus.
Management tightened FY26 guidance to constant currency growth of c.6% (consensus 6.1%). GS notes this implies acceleration to c.5.5% growth in Q4, helped by the recently acquired Neurotech.
Management lowered its market growth expectation from 3-4% to 3%.

Constant currency margin expansion guidance narrowed from +90-190bps to +100-150bps, with a +10bps FX tailwind. The midpoint implies a core EBIT margin of 21.1% (consensus 21.2%), a lower midpoint than before despite more favorable tariff expectations ($40m net headwind versus $40-90m previously).
Core EPS growth guidance is 12-14% versus 12-15% previously, with a +160bps FX tailwind. GS estimates the midpoint implies core diluted EPS of $3.51 (consensus $3.49).

GS expects softer-than-expected revenue growth to dominate investor discussion. The Q4 implied growth is slightly below Alcon's mid-term guidance of 6-8%, and that includes M&A tailwind. Focus will shift to FY27e, where consensus assumes growth of 5.9%.

Surgical grew +4% c.FX (consensus +4.9%) with $1,480m sales broadly in line. Implantables fell 2% c.FX (consensus flat) to $422m, as strength in PanOptix Pro and outside-US growth was offset by competitive pressure in US implantables.
Equipment grew +11% (consensus 14.4%) to $269m, 2% below consensus, reflecting launches including the Unity platform and Valeda.

Vision Care grew +6% c.FX (consensus +7.1%) to $1,237m, -1% versus consensus. Contact lenses grew +5% (consensus 5.1%) to $737m on premium mix and price increases, partly offset by declines in legacy products.
Ocular Health grew +8% (consensus 10.0%) to $500m, 1% below consensus. Dry eye products including SYSTANE and TRYPTYR were partly offset by contact lens care declines.
GS rates Alcon Buy with 12-month price targets of CHF 69 / US$83 (upside 11.5% / 12.1%). The stock trades on 16.3x 12m forward P/E.

market_movers.rationale: Buy reiterated after Q3 26 with a $83 target (CHF 69 on the Swiss listing), 12.1% upside from $74.06. Target blends DCF and 19.0x P/E multiples at 50% weight each.

earnings_insights: Alcon Q3 26 (reported 10 Nov 2026): constant currency revenue growth 5.2% versus consensus +6%. Reported revenue $2,717m versus GSe $2,738m and Visible Alpha consensus $2,748m (-1.1% versus consensus).
Q3 26 core gross profit $1,786m, margin 65.7% versus GSe 66.2% and consensus 64.6%. Core EBIT $591m (21.8% of revenue) versus GSe $592m and consensus $590m. The text cites core EBIT as $592m.
Q3 26 core net income $442m versus consensus $431m. Core basic EPS 0.92 reported versus GSe 0.89 and consensus 0.87 (+6.2% versus consensus).

Q3 26 division detail, reported versus consensus: Implantables $422m (-2.3%), Consumables $789m (+1.1%), Equipment $269m (-2.3%), Total Surgical $1,480m (-0.4%), Contact lenses $737m (-0.7%), Ocular Health $500m (-1.2%), Total Vision Care $1,237m (-0.9%).

FY26 guidance (company, tightened): constant currency growth c.6% (consensus 6.1%), constant currency margin expansion +100-150bps (previously +90-190bps), core EPS growth 12-14% (previously 12-15%), net tariff headwind $40m (previously $40-90m).
GS FY26E estimates: revenue $11,044.7m, EBIT $2,359.1m, EPS $3.51. FY27E: revenue $11,720.2m, EBIT $2,526.8m, EPS $3.85. FY28E EPS $4.46. Consensus FY27e revenue growth is 5.9%.
risk_factors: Soft end-market demand for ophthalmic procedures.
US or broader consumer slowdown hitting consumer-facing businesses.
Failure to execute on product launches, or launch delays affecting growth phasing.
Greater-than-expected margin pressure from tariffs, transactional FX, or unforeseen expenses to support launches.
